Used to form adjectives meaning resembling or having characteristics of the related term. From earlier -uous , alteration of -wose , -wos , a variant of -wise , from Middle English -wise , -wis , -wys , from Old English -wīs (“-wise”), under the influence of Etymology 2. More at -wise. Suffix Forming a placename or a surname derived therefrom and denoting or connoting a hill or mountain; sometimes (as in estate names) used more for euphony and connotation than for geomorphic denotation. Word formation in English using the suffix to name towns and family estates was most productive in the mid-19th through mid-20th centuries. From French -mont , from French mont (“hill, mountain”).
